$\mathrm { T A T - R a s G A P } _ { 3 1 7 - 3 2 6 }$ is a retro-inverso peptide (i.e., synthesized with D-amino-acids in the opposite direction compared to the natural sequence). The TAT moiety corresponds to amino-acids 48–57 of the HIV TAT protein (RRRQRRKKRG) and the $\mathrm { R a s G A P } _ { 3 1 7 - 3 2 6 }$ moiety corresponds to amino-acids 317–326 of the human RasGAP protein (DTRLNTVWMW). These two moieties are separated by two glycine linker residues in the $\mathrm { T A T - R a s \mathrm { - } G A P } _ { 3 1 7 - 3 2 6 }$ peptide. $\mathrm { T A T - R a s G A P } _ { 3 1 7 - 3 2 6 }$ (W317A) has the tryptophan at position 317 mutated into an alanine. These peptides were synthesized at the department of biochemistry, University of Lausanne, Switzerland, using FMOC technology, purified by HPLC and tested by mass spectrometry.
